options.description: Asks with plain lines in and lines out rather than a region that redraws, for a screen reader: the question is written once, what is typed is echoed where it is typed, and nothing already written is ever moved or erased.
options.name: accessible

options.description: Whether Escape leaves the prompt to go back a step. Defaults to `false`, where Escape does nothing, as it always has.
options.name: back

options.description: Days to mark, as `Date`s. Only the day is read, in local time. A marked day carries a `*` after its number, so it survives a terminal with no colour, and the `sigil-calendar-highlight` role besides.
options.name: highlight

options.description: The day the cursor starts on. Defaults to today. One outside `min` and `max` is moved to the nearest bound.
options.name: initial

options.description: The language month and weekday names are written in, as a BCP 47 tag. Defaults to the locale the app's catalog resolved, else the system's.
options.default: the locale the app's catalog resolved
options.name: locale

options.description: The latest day that can be picked, inclusive.
options.name: max

options.description: The earliest day that can be picked, inclusive.
options.name: min

options.description: The input router to read keys through. One is built if not given.
options.name: router

options.description: Gives the prompt up when this aborts, the way Ctrl-C does.
options.name: signal

options.description: Where keys come from. Defaults to the terminal's input.
options.name: stdin

options.description: An answer to start from: the day the cursor starts on, beating `initial` and pulled into `min` and `max` the same way. One that is not a valid date is dropped rather than refused.
options.name: value

options.description: The weekday a row starts on: 0 is Sunday, 1 is Monday, up to 6. Defaults to what the locale says, and to Sunday where the runtime cannot say.
options.name: weekStart
